ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — John Locke Synthetic CCD

text.paragraph: Primary care visit for a lifelong cough with wheeze and breathlessness, worse in city air and by open fires, in a never-smoker. Concerns: He has coughed for twenty years, and the city air leaves him unable to breathe; he wants to be able to do his work there; He wonders whether this is the consumption that his father and brother had; He asks whether the fire in his study is part of the problem. [S]

tr.td: Albuterol 90 mcg/actuation inhaler, two puffs every 4 hours as needed while tests are done; hold for 6 hours before spirometry
Two puffs every 4 hours as needed
Budesonide-formoterol 160/4.5 mcg inhaler as maintenance and reliever (GINA track 1, step 4): two inhalations twice daily and one inhalation as needed for symptoms, no more than 12 inhalations a day
Two inhalations twice daily plus one as needed; no more than 12 a day
Tiotropium 2.5 mcg/actuation soft-mist inhaler, two inhalations once daily (add-on long-acting muscarinic antagonist, GINA step 5)
Acetaminophen 500 mg oral tablet, one or two tablets every 6 hours as needed for aches or fever, no more than 3 g a day
One or two tablets every 6 hours as needed; no more than six tablets a day

list.item: Chronic cough with wheeze and breathlessness since his late thirties, worse every winter and within a day of any stay in the city or by an open fire, better in warm weather and country air; night cough two or three times a week this winter; under evaluation: resolved, confirmed [S]
Long exposure to urban air pollution (decades in a large city with heavy traffic and coal and wood burning) and to indoor solid-fuel smoke from open coal and wood fires at home: active, confirmed [S]

Asthma with persistent airflow limitation, type 2 (eosinophilic) phenotype, in a never-smoker: post-bronchodilator FEV1/FVC 0.62, FEV1 62 percent predicted rising 380 mL after albuterol, FeNO 41 ppb, eosinophils 0.46 x 10^3/uL, IgE 186 IU/mL, normal DLCO, no emphysema on CT; aggravated by air pollution and indoor smoke; not COPD: active, confirmed [S]

Acute viral upper respiratory infection (common cold) with a yellow-zone asthma flare: peak flow 68 percent of personal best, managed with extra as-needed budesonide-formoterol by his action plan, without oral corticosteroids; resolved: resolved, confirmed [S]

tr.td: Chronic cough with wheeze and breathlessness since his late thirties, worse every winter and within a day of any stay in the city or by an open fire, better in warm weather and country air; night cough two or three times a week this winter; under evaluation
S — Synthetic presenting problem echoing his documented lifelong cough and breathlessness in London's coal smoke; superseded by the diagnosis at the second visit.
Long exposure to urban air pollution (decades in a large city with heavy traffic and coal and wood burning) and to indoor solid-fuel smoke from open coal and wood fires at home
S — Synthetic modern exposure echoing the coal smoke that he, Sydenham, and Lady Masham blamed for his cough; no historical level of exposure is asserted.

Asthma with persistent airflow limitation, type 2 (eosinophilic) phenotype, in a never-smoker: post-bronchodilator FEV1/FVC 0.62, FEV1 62 percent predicted rising 380 mL after albuterol, FeNO 41 ppb, eosinophils 0.46 x 10^3/uL, IgE 186 IU/mL, normal DLCO, no emphysema on CT; aggravated by air pollution and indoor smoke; not COPD
S — Synthetic modern diagnosis. His lifelong cough and breathlessness worse in coal smoke are documented (D); calling them asthma is a modern retrospective reading (R).

Acute viral upper respiratory infection (common cold) with a yellow-zone asthma flare: peak flow 68 percent of personal best, managed with extra as-needed budesonide-formoterol by his action plan, without oral corticosteroids; resolved
S — Synthetic intercurrent illness at an unscheduled visit; it echoes, without asserting, his documented autumn chest troubles (CLM-0014).

list.item: Occupation: philosopher and author; trained as a physician (bachelor of medicine) and still gives occasional informal medical advice; serves part-time on a government appeals board, which takes him into the city for a few days at a time [S]

Home: for a year has lodged with long-standing friends in an old country house about 25 miles from the city; his study and bedroom are heated by open fires that burn coal and wood, and he reads by the fire most evenings; no gas cooking in his rooms; no damp or mould; no pets or birds [S]

Exposure history: about 30 years living and working in a large city with heavy traffic and winter coal and wood smoke, in flats near main roads; breathless within a day of each return; no occupational dust, fume, or chemical exposure [S]
Never smoker; never vaped; no secondhand tobacco smoke at home; a glass of wine with dinner a few times a week (AUDIT-C 2); no other substances [S]
Never married; no children; close to the household he lives with; walks most days in good weather [S]

tr.td: Primary care visit for a lifelong cough with wheeze and breathlessness, worse in city air and by open fires, in a never-smoker
Two-week review of lung function and blood tests, diagnosis, start of treatment, and pulmonology consultation
Twelve-week asthma review with repeat spirometry after pulmonary rehabilitation
Asthma review two weeks after a cold with a yellow-zone flare
Same-day sick visit for a cold with a yellow-zone asthma flare

code.displayName: Periodic reevaluation and management of healthy individual

tr.td: Diagnostic workup: spirometry before and after bronchodilator, FeNO, DLCO, blood count with eosinophils, total IgE, alpha-1 antitrypsin, NT-proBNP, interferon-gamma release assay, chest X-ray, and CT of the chest if airflow limitation persists after bronchodilator; albuterol withheld for 6 hours before testing
GL-CMID-2026, GL-GINA-2025, GL-NAEPP-2020, GL-GOLD-2025, GL-ATS-ERS-PFT-2022, GL-ATS-RACE-2023

Exposure reduction from today: no open coal or wood fires in his rooms (electric or heat-pump heating instead); a portable HEPA air cleaner sized for his study and bedroom; daily check of the air quality index, with city trips and outdoor exertion avoided on alert days; a well-fitted N95 respirator on unavoidable high-pollution days; quieter routes away from main roads
GL-WHO-AQG-2021, GL-ERS-AIR-2020, GL-AIRNOW-AQI, GL-EPA-AIRCLEAN, GL-CMID-2026, GL-GINA-2025, GL-NAEPP-2020
Pulmonology consultation on the diagnosis (asthma, COPD, or both), the need for CT, treatment, and pulmonary rehabilitation

Shared decision on treatment: budesonide-formoterol 160/4.5 mcg as maintenance and reliever, two inhalations twice daily plus one as needed, no more than 12 a day; albuterol stopped; inhaler technique taught and checked at every visit; a written asthma action plan
Pulmonary rehabilitation: an eight-week, twice-weekly program of supervised exercise training and education, with a six-minute walk test before and after
Vaccinations: pneumococcal conjugate vaccine PCV20 at the diagnosis visit; influenza, COVID-19, and RSV vaccines in the autumn; recombinant zoster vaccine

Monitoring: Asthma Control Test, inhaler technique, adherence, reliever use, and exposures at every visit; spirometry and FeNO 3 months after starting treatment, then every 1 to 2 years; home peak flow diary

Add-on tiotropium 2.5 mcg soft-mist inhaler, two inhalations once daily, for persistent symptoms and airflow limitation on medium-dose budesonide-formoterol; written action plan updated with peak-flow zones from his personal best of 440 L/min
After any flare: a review within one week, booked by the clinic when he calls or is seen for the flare
Cause of the cough and breathlessness established by the second visit
Asthma with persistent airflow limitation confirmed by spirometry, FeNO, eosinophils, DLCO, and CT; tuberculosis, alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency, and heart failure excluded
Asthma well controlled (Asthma Control Test 20 or more) with no flare needing oral corticosteroids
ACT 21 at the last visit; one yellow-zone flare with a cold, managed by the action plan without oral corticosteroids
No indoor solid-fuel smoke and less outdoor pollution exposure
Open fires out of use since intake; HEPA air cleaner in his study and bedroom; air quality alerts followed
Six-minute walk distance improved by at least 30 m after pulmonary rehabilitation
430 m before and 505 m after an eight-week program

list.item: Independent in all activities of daily living; walks about a mile on the level at his own pace, but stops on hills and after one flight of stairs this winter; cannot stay in the city more than a day or two without severe breathlessness [S]
Alert, articulate, and good-humored; mood "tired of being driven out of town"; thought process orderly; no anxiety or low mood beyond frustration (PHQ-2 1) [S]
